title: Why AI Agents Should Have Their Own Sandbox — Philipp Schmid, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: Philipp Schmid demos Gemini's managed agent sandboxes: each agent request spins up a persistent cloud sandbox (8 vCPU/16GB) where the agent loop, tool calls, file writes, and MCP servers all run server-side, with skills/AGENTS.md auto-loaded from the filesystem. Environments are reusable across turns and shareable between agents, and agents can build their own preconfigured environments that later agents start from.

takeaways.technique: Persistent per-agent sandbox with server-side agent loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Each agent request starts a managed cloud sandbox; the entire agent loop (reasoning, bash, function calls, MCP) runs inside it rather than on the client, and the environment persists across turns.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have like this agent loop completely on our server ... everything runs inside that remote sandbox
takeaways.numbers: 8 vCPU, 16 GB memory, Ubuntu; first request ~7-10s to start environment

takeaways.technique: Shared environment for multi-agent context passing
takeaways.what_they_do: Multiple agents can work in the same sandbox and share context through the filesystem, and sub-agents can pick up work another agent left behind.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can share environments between different agents ... they can share context through the file system

takeaways.technique: Filesystem-native skills + AGENTS.md auto-loaded into system prompt
takeaways.what_they_do: Skills stored in a skills directory and an AGENTS.md file are automatically picked up and appended to the system instruction at environment startup.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you store skills inside the skills directory, it will automatically picked up ... agents MD file ... automatically appended to the system instruction

takeaways.technique: Agents build their own reusable base environment
takeaways.what_they_do: An agent scaffolds an environment (install GitHub CLI, add skills, sanity checks), returns an environment ID, and future agents start from that preconfigured snapshot.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can use the agent to create its own environment ... every time I call this new agent, it will start from that already pre-loaded, preconfigured environment

takeaways.technique: Server-side state / step timeline instead of user-model turns
takeaways.what_they_do: API tracks interaction state server-side and models actions as typed steps (function result, thought) rather than user/model turns, so follow-ups just pass the prior ID.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we moved away from like those turns into steps ... every action or generation is its own type

takeaways.technique: MCP servers run inside the sandbox
takeaways.what_they_do: Remote MCP servers can be connected and local MCP servers can run inside the agent's environment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can also connect remote MCP servers or run uh local MCP servers inside of that environment
